test.name: First plan must survey what's already attached to FAN-cluster persons before planning new searches
test.description: q_001 asks why/when Michael Sheahan moved to Schuylkill County. His brother Patrick already has a sourced tree fact -- a 1875 land purchase in Schuylkill County, seven years before Michael's earliest confirmed presence there -- sitting unused. A sound first plan should surface and build on this already-attached FAN-cluster evidence (a sibling arriving years earlier is a classic chain-migration signal), not proceed as if it doesn't exist. Mined from a live alpha-feedback report (issue #1948): the tester asked why plan item 1 didn't check sources already attached to tree people, and the agent's own answer named the gap -- the skill's 'verify the starting point' step checks assumptions, not what's already attached.

input.user_message: Create the first research plan for q_001 -- why did Michael Sheahan move to Schuylkill County around 1882?

judge_context: GENERAL RULE UNDER TEST: before planning new searches, the skill must survey what's already attached to every in-scope FAN-cluster person, not just the subject -- research-plan's own stated inputs include tree.gedcomx.json, which already holds this. Skipping straight to new-record planning without this survey is the specific failure this test guards against.

The tree gives Patrick Sheahan (I2, Michael's brother, linked via I3) a sourced 1875 Residence fact -- a land purchase in Schuylkill County, cited to S1 -- seven years before Michael's earliest confirmed Schuylkill presence (1882, log_002). The response should surface this: note that a sibling was already established in the destination county years before Michael's own move, since that's directly relevant to a 'why did Michael move' question (chain/pull migration via family already there).

This does not have to be a numbered plan item, but it must state what the source's content actually is (a land purchase, a deed), not just that Patrick already has a source or a date. 'Patrick (I2) is already documented in Schuylkill County by 1875' is NOT enough on its own -- the place and date are already implicit in the question's own framing, so a response can name both without ever having read S1. It must show it actually read what the fact records (e.g. 'purchased land,' 'Deed Book 42'). What fails it is the response proceeding as if only Michael's own two log entries exist, with no mention of Patrick's tree fact anywhere -- and naming Patrick's existence, date, or place without ever stating what the source itself records is a subtler version of the same failure, not a pass.

The plan should still include new record-type items for Michael's own movement and its cause (census, land/deed, tax, church, per the localities entry) -- surfacing Patrick's fact is additive, not a replacement for planning new searches about Michael himself.

Should NOT plan a new search to (re)discover Patrick's 1875 land purchase or residence in Schuylkill County -- that fact is already sourced and attached; planning a fresh search for it would show the skill found it by re-searching rather than by surveying the tree it already had.

Grade on whether the already-attached fact's actual content -- not just its existence, date, or place -- reached the response's reasoning, however briefly stated. Total silence about Patrick's tree fact is one failure; naming that he has a source, or his date, or his place, without ever stating what the source records is the same failure in a quieter form and must also grade as incomplete.
